name: RAKBANK Titanium Credit Card

primary_uses: Statement credit via the RAKBANK mobile app, minimum AED 100; unredeemed cashback expires 15 months after it is earned

benefits: No annual fee
data_caveat: PUBLISHABLE as of 2026-08-08 (D16). The hold was lifted because the exact evidence its own resolution condition demanded was supplied: RAKBANK's product page stating per-category cashback percentages AND their monthly caps TOGETHER, plus the separation of promotional from standing terms. Three independent checks passed. (1) CAP ARITHMETIC CLOSES: the six stated per-category caps (supermarket 100, dining 100, cinema 100, video streaming 100, e-wallet retail 100, non-e-wallet retail 100) sum to exactly the AED 600 total monthly cap already recorded from the separately-supplied schedule - two sources agreeing on a figure neither derives from the other. (2) PROMOTIONAL vs STANDING is now separable: the AED 500 welcome bonus is explicitly dated 15 Jul - 15 Sep 2026, while the cashback percentages carry no date, which retires the leading 'the headline rates are promotional' hypothesis. (3) The AED 2,000 minimum monthly spend is restated against every category. FIXED IN THE SAME PASS: the non-e-wallet retail rate is capped at AED 100/mo and the engine was modelling it as an UNCAPPED base rate; it is now encoded as `all_other_spend` with that cap, which also stops the virtual uncapped base being synthesised. RESIDUAL, deliberately conservative: the 0.25% low-earn bucket is NOT mentioned on the product page and rests solely on the 1 Sep 2024 schedule - kept, because dropping it would raise the card's score and absence from a marketing page is not evidence of absence. The 2% e-wallet retail tier is still NOT encoded (it and standard retail both map to canonical `other`, so encoding it would shadow the 1% and overstate; D14 rule: encode the lower), so e-wallet spend remains understated. PRIOR HOLD, retained for the record: it read a 4.31% net annual return on a mid-range profile with NO annual fee, driven by 50% cashback on cinemas and video streaming; its AED 600 total monthly cap implies up to AED 7,200/year free-for-life. That exceeds the study's own bar ("a UAE credit card returning >8% of total spend does not exist"), and admitting both cards moved the PUBLISHABLE median optimal return from 3.98% to 6.49% of spend with p90 at 7.80% - a 63% jump in the headline caused by two cards. The encoding was re-checked line by line against the supplied schedule and matches it, so the doubt is about the SOURCE, not the transcription. MOST LIKELY EXPLANATIONS, in order: the 10%/50% headline rates are promotional or introductory rather than standing; the per-category caps are lower than recorded; or the rates apply only above a spend tier not captured here. NEEDED TO RESOLVE: the RAKBANK Key Fact Statement or Cashback Information leaflet showing per-category cashback percentages AND their monthly caps together, plus whether the schedule is promotional. Until then this card is scored (its strings are sound) but must not carry a published claim. RESOLVED 2026-08-05 (D15) from the RAKBANK cashback schedule effective 1 Sep 2024, supplied directly; the live page publishes only 'up to' values and defers to a leaflet/Key Fact Statement. All five ceilings are now certain rates. BASE CORRECTED 2% -> 1%: the advertised 'up to 2%' is the E-WALLET rate; standard Other Retail earns 1%. The 2% e-wallet tier is NOT encoded because both it and standard retail map to canonical `other`, so encoding 2% would shadow the 1% and overstate; per the D14 rule the lower rate is used. E-wallet spend is therefore understated. NEW: the 0.25% low-earn bucket (charities, government, bill payments, schools, education, transit, transport, telecom, real estate, petrol) was absent entirely - previously that spend earned the base rate, a 4x overstatement. overall_cap set to the stated AED 600 total monthly cap (AED 400 premium + AED 200 retail), which was null before, so the card was uncapped in aggregate. Redemption needs a minimum AED 100 balance; cashback expires 15 months from earning.

name: RAKBANK World Cashback Credit Card

primary_uses: Statement credit; unredeemed cashback expires 15 months after it is earned

benefits: Mastercard lounge and travel benefits subject to conditions
data_caveat: PUBLISHABLE as of 2026-08-08 (D16). The hold was lifted because the exact evidence its own resolution condition demanded was supplied: RAKBANK's product page stating per-category cashback percentages AND their monthly caps TOGETHER, plus the separation of promotional from standing terms. Three independent checks passed. (1) CAP ARITHMETIC CLOSES: the five stated per-category caps (travel & hotels 400, supermarket 300, dining 300, e-wallet retail 150, non-e-wallet retail 100) sum to exactly the AED 1,250 total monthly cap already recorded from the separately-supplied schedule - two sources agreeing on a figure neither derives from the other. (2) PROMOTIONAL vs STANDING is now separable: the AED 750 welcome bonus is explicitly dated 15 Jul - 15 Sep 2026, while the cashback percentages carry no date, which retires the leading 'the headline rates are promotional' hypothesis. (3) The AED 10,000 minimum monthly spend is restated against every category. FIXED IN THE SAME PASS: the non-e-wallet retail rate is capped at AED 100/mo and the engine was modelling it as an UNCAPPED base rate applying to every non-bonus category; `other_retail` (which reached canonical `other` only) is replaced by `all_other_spend` at 1% capped 100, which is the faithful catch-all and stops the virtual uncapped base being synthesised. RESIDUAL, deliberately conservative: the 0.25% low-earn bucket is NOT mentioned on the product page and rests solely on the 1 Sep 2024 schedule - kept, because dropping it would raise the card's score and absence from a marketing page is not evidence of absence. The 3% e-wallet retail tier is still NOT encoded (D14 rule: encode the lower), so e-wallet spend remains understated. NOT MODELLED, both are PERKS rather than earn rates and must never become categories: 12 months of Careem Plus (10% back on up to 10 rides, free delivery) and 50% off up to 4 VOX cinema tickets per month. PRIOR HOLD, retained for the record: it read a 5.12% net annual return on a mid-range profile, and its schedule implies up to AED 15,000/year (the AED 1,250 total monthly cap) against the AED 120,000 annual spend it requires to unlock - 12.5%. That exceeds the study's own bar ("a UAE credit card returning >8% of total spend does not exist"), and admitting both cards moved the PUBLISHABLE median optimal return from 3.98% to 6.49% of spend with p90 at 7.80% - a 63% jump in the headline caused by two cards. The encoding was re-checked line by line against the supplied schedule and matches it, so the doubt is about the SOURCE, not the transcription. MOST LIKELY EXPLANATIONS, in order: the 10%/50% headline rates are promotional or introductory rather than standing; the per-category caps are lower than recorded; or the rates apply only above a spend tier not captured here. NEEDED TO RESOLVE: the RAKBANK Key Fact Statement or Cashback Information leaflet showing per-category cashback percentages AND their monthly caps together, plus whether the schedule is promotional. Until then this card is scored (its strings are sound) but must not carry a published claim. RESOLVED 2026-08-05 (D15) from the RAKBANK cashback schedule effective 1 Sep 2024, supplied directly; the live page publishes only 'up to' values. All ceilings are now certain rates. BASE CORRECTED 3% -> 1%: the advertised 'up to 3%' is the E-WALLET rate; standard Other Retail earns 1%. The 3% e-wallet tier is NOT encoded - it and standard retail both map to canonical `other`, so it would shadow the 1% and overstate (D14 rule: encode the lower). E-wallet spend is understated. NEW: the 0.25% low-earn bucket (charities, government, bill payments, schools, education, transit, transport, telecom, real estate, petrol) was absent entirely, so that spend previously earned the base rate - a 4x overstatement. overall_cap corrected 1100 -> 1250 (the stated total monthly cap). Requires AED 10,000 monthly spend to unlock; redemption needs a minimum AED 300 balance.
